deviations: The brief's correlations r12 = r13 = 0.90, r23 = 0.50 do not form a positive-definite correlation matrix (determinant -0.06), so no data set can have them. Smallest fix keeping r23 = 0.50 and lambda2^2 = lambda3^2 = 0.50: r12 = r13 = 0.85 (determinant 0.0275). Closed form becomes lambda1^2 = 1.445, theta1 = -0.445.
expectedTruths: Sample correlations of data.csv are exactly r12 = 0.85, r13 = 0.85, r23 = 0.50 (unit variances, zero means, N-1 divisor).

The one-factor model with 3 indicators is just identified (6 moments, 6 parameters, df = 0). Its exact solution on the correlation metric: lambda1^2 = r12*r13/r23 = 1.445, lambda2^2 = r12*r23/r13 = 0.50, lambda3^2 = r13*r23/r12 = 0.50; theta1 = 1 - 1.445 = -0.445, theta2 = 0.50, theta3 = 0.50.

theta1 < 0 is a Heywood case (standardised loading of h1 = sqrt(1.445) = 1.202082 > 1). An engine must surface a negative-variance / inadmissible-solution warning (estimation.admissible = false) and must not present the result as a clean fit; chi-square = 0 with df = 0 carries no evidence of fit.
With the N-divisor covariance (lavaan default) the unstandardised theta1 is -0.445 * 199/200; the standardised solution is unchanged.
